title: Escape terminal control bytes in wt list's Summary column
body:
`wt list`'s Summary column printed the first line of the configured `[commit.generation]` command's output without escaping. #4605 made the Message column run commit subjects through `escape_controls` before truncating, but the Summary column was left out. So an ESC, BEL or CR in the LLM's reply, such as an OSC 52 clipboard sequence echoed from a diff it was asked to summarize, went straight to the terminal and also threw off the width math that keeps columns aligned. The path is `compute_summary_generate` → `generate_summary_core` → `execute_llm_command`, which only trims the output, then `render_cell`.

This PR escapes the summary in the Summary arm of `render_cell`, as the Message arm already does. JSON output still carries the raw text, matching #4605.

`test_summary_column_rendering` gets a fourth case: a summary containing an OSC 52 sequence now renders as visible `\u{1b}…\u{7}` escapes. Without the fix, that case fails.

The picker's Summary preview tab renders the full generated summary through its own path, and this PR doesn't change it.

Found during the nightly survey by reading the code, not from a user report.

title: Stop the fsmonitor orphan sweep killing submodule daemons
body:
The orphan fsmonitor sweep that runs after `wt remove` and `wt merge` (`run_internal_sweep` → `reap_orphan_fsmonitor_daemons` → `classify_orphans`) treated any daemon as a class-2 orphan when its git-dir sat under the repo's git-common-dir but wasn't a live worktree's git-dir. Submodule git-dirs also live under the common dir, at `.git/modules/<name>`, and `git worktree list` never reports them. So with `core.fsmonitor=true` set globally, every sweep sent SIGTERM and then SIGKILL to the daemons serving live submodules. That breaks the module's own rule that a daemon serving a live checkout is never reaped. Git respawns the daemon on the next command, so the damage is a lost cache, not lost data.

This PR limits class 2 to the git-dirs this repo's own worktrees use: the common dir itself, and `<common-dir>/worktrees/<name>`. Everything else nested in the common dir is spared, the same way daemons for other repositories already are.

`classifies_each_orphan_class_and_spares_others` now also has a submodule daemon and a daemon for a submodule's linked worktree. Under the old `starts_with` check, both would have been selected. Locally, the fsmonitor unit tests and clippy pass. The one other failure, `start_fsmonitor_daemon_skips_fork_when_daemon_answers`, also fails on `main` here, because this sandbox blocks `AF_UNIX` sockets.

title: skills(writing-user-outputs): fold a second suggestion into the existing hint
body:
`writing-user-outputs` explained how to join two suggestions into one hint, but never said to join them instead of stacking a second hint line. This edit states that rule. The rule covers suggestions only. Context hints already sit beside a suggestion hint in `GitError::WorktreeRemovalFailed` ("Remaining in directory") and `GitError::WorktreeCreationFailed` ("Failed command"), and those stay as they are.

title: ci: stop fast-checks saving the shared Linux rust cache
body:
On main, `fast-checks` and `test (linux)` both save the `v1-rust-shared-Linux-x64-*` rust cache. When the key changes (a `Cargo.lock` or toolchain change), `fast-checks` finishes minutes earlier and reserves the key with a cache built only for lockfile, doctest, and rustdoc. `test (linux)` then fails to save, and later Linux runs restore that partial cache until the key changes again. This PR passes `save-cache: "false"` to `fast-checks`, as `collect-affected`, `affected-tests`, and `release-target` already do, so `test` stays the only job that saves the cache, as the `test-setup` input description says.

Two recent main runs show the race:

- [41815243371](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/actions/runs/41815243371): `fast-checks` started `Saving cache` at 10:37:15. `test (linux)` reached its save at 10:44:25 and got `Failed to save: Unable to reserve cache with key v1-rust-shared-Linux-x64-867d58cd-d69464dc, another job may be creating this cache.`
- [41832227759](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/actions/runs/41832227759): the same thing happened with key `…-659612d8`.

When the key is unchanged, every job restores with `full match: true` and none saves, so this only matters on key changes. CI is the only test for a workflow-only change.

The nightly `full-tests` job also keeps the default. It runs the same full suite, so a cache it saves isn't partial, and I left it alone.

title: fix(switch): use a GitHub PR URL's host for gh api
body:
`wt switch https://host/owner/repo/pull/N` asked `gh api` with no `--hostname`, so the lookup went to gh's default host. An Enterprise URL then 404'd when the git remote was github.com, even though gh was logged in on the URL's host.

When `forge.hostname` is unset, the `/pull/N` URL's host is now passed as `--hostname` if `gh auth token` succeeds for it. `pr:N` still follows the remote, and the 404 hint is unchanged.

Checked with the new switch cases (logged in and not), the existing enterprise-remote regression, the URL-host unit test, `cargo test --doc`, and `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`.

Refs #4709

title: fix(completion): filter PowerShell completions by prefix
body: In PowerShell, `wt switch feat<Tab>` replaces `feat` with whichever branch is listed first (e.g. `main`) instead of a branch starting with `feat`. The value completers return every candidate so fish and zsh can do their own matching, and only bash gets a prefix filter (#1622), but clap's PowerShell completer doesn't filter on the typed word either. This applies the existing filter for `COMPLETE=powershell` too, and the cross-shell filtering contract test now covers powershell. Ran `cargo test --test integration -- completion::`, and checked `TabExpansion2` with the shell integration loaded in pwsh 7.6.9 and Windows PowerShell 5.1.

title: fix(docs): restore 48px favicon and apple-touch-icon links
body:
The Astro rebuild (#3866) moved `favicon-48.png` and `apple-touch-icon.png` into `docs/public/` but dropped the `<link>` tags that #627 had added to the old Zola base template. Since then every page emits only `<link rel="shortcut icon" href="/favicon.png">` (32×32). This PR adds the two links back through Starlight's `head` option, so the larger icons are discoverable again.

This restores metadata. It doesn't fix the generic globe in Google Search (#4718), because nothing establishes the cause. [Google's favicon guidance](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/favicon-in-search) accepts a square icon of at least 8×8 and supports `shortcut icon`, so the existing 32×32 icon is not inherently ineligible. Advertising a 48×48 icon follows Google's recommendation for a larger size, but whether it changes the search result is unverified.

A new `built-site.test.mjs` case requires both links on every rendered page, so they can't drop out silently again. It fails on the current build and passes with this change. `npm run check`, `npm test`, and the rest of `test:site` pass locally. The exception is the existing social-card asset check, which needs the `worktrunk-assets` clone that CI fetches and this sandbox doesn't have.

title: fix(wt-switch-create): leave the current worktree session before entering by path
body:
A session already in a worktree can enter only a worktree under its repo's `.claude/worktrees/`, so `/wt-switch-create` step 3's `EnterWorktree({path})` always hit the managed-location rejection there. The `cd` recovery then left Claude Code tracking the old worktree: its Bash guard, session exit, and `ExitWorktree` all kept acting on it. Step 3 now calls `ExitWorktree({action: "keep"})` before entering. That keeps the old worktree on disk and makes the entry a first entry. With no repo argument the session enters from where leaving put it, with no `cd`. With a repo argument, `cd <repo>` follows as before.

This applies the patch from the issue verbatim: `skills/wt-switch-create/SKILL.md` and `rationale.md`, plus the `plugins/worktrunk/skills/` mirror regenerated by `test_docs_are_in_sync`. That includes the follow-on edits: the handback names the worktree the session left, `git stash pop` waits until the session is in the new worktree, Cleanup covers the worktree that was left, and rationale.md corrects the rejection list and the Known limits entry.

Verification: the behavior depends on Claude Code's live `EnterWorktree`/`ExitWorktree` tools, which CI can't run. The evidence is the issue's live checks against Claude Code 2.1.316 and wt v0.81.0, including a headless A/B where every already-in-a-worktree scenario went from 0/3 (0/2 for `--worktree`) to 3/3 and plain sessions stayed 3/3. Locally, the patch applied cleanly at `d022f7683` and `test_docs_are_in_sync` passes with the regenerated mirror.

title: fix(switch): pass a GitHub Enterprise remote's host to gh api when gh is logged in to it
body:
`gh api` doesn't take its host from the repository. Without `--hostname` it uses gh's default host, which is github.com once more than one host is logged in. `fetch_pr_info` passed `--hostname` only when `forge.hostname` was set, so on a GitHub Enterprise remote `wt switch pr:N` and `wt switch <PR URL>` asked github.com for the PR and got a 404. With no `forge.hostname`, the lookup now passes the GitHub remote's host as `--hostname` if `gh auth token --hostname <host>` succeeds (a local check, no network; `choose_pr_forge` already uses the same check). An SSH alias such as `github-personal` has no gh login, so it still goes to gh's default host. That keeps the #1790 fix in place, the one #1826 made by removing host detection. A configured `forge.hostname` still takes priority. github.com remotes skip the check, so they behave as before.

`test_switch_pr_enterprise_remote_passes_hostname` uses an `https://github.example.com/...` remote and a mock `gh`. When `gh` is logged in to that host, the test expects `--hostname github.example.com` on the `api` call; it failed before this change and passes now. When `gh` isn't logged in to it, the test expects no `--hostname` flag. The existing `pr` integration tests pass.

Not changed here: the issue's second suggestion, a 404 hint that names `forge.hostname`. That case still applies when `gh` has no login for the Enterprise host. Whether to add that output is up to a maintainer. A PR URL's own host is also not used yet. In the reported setup the remote's host matches the URL's, so this change fixes that case.

After two quick `alt-r` refreshes in the `wt switch` picker, a superseded refresh whose skeleton lands last could overwrite the layout that `alt-x` uses, so a later `alt-x` rendered its `/ branch` row on the old column grid. `provide_layout` wrote the session-shared `layout_slot` unconditionally. `on_skeleton` already guards the other session-shared writes (`shared_items` and the shortcut table) with `spawn_gen.is_current()`. title: Ship Codex activity-marker hooks as a separate hooks-only plugin
body:
Codex 0.164+ ties plugin hook approval to a fingerprint of every file in the plugin directory. The `worktrunk` plugin keeps the skills mirror and docs next to its four marker hooks, so almost every release made Codex ask users to approve hooks that hadn't changed (#4654). This PR moves those hooks into a second plugin, `worktrunk-markers`. It holds only its manifest and copies of the `wt.sh`/`wt.cmd` shims, so its fingerprint changes only when the hooks or shims change. `wt config plugins codex install` adds both plugins, and `uninstall` removes both.

The design follows the live test max-sixty posted in #4654 on Codex 0.166.0. A skill or README change re-prompted the combined plugin but not a hooks-only one. That test also listed four requirements, and this PR covers each one:

- **Existing installs.** When an existing user's `worktrunk` plugin updates, its hooks go away silently. The installer adds the markers plugin, and the Codex section of the agent-integration docs now names `codex plugin add worktrunk-markers@worktrunk` for older installs.
- **No Claude hooks warning.** The `worktrunk` Codex manifest keeps `"hooks": {"hooks": {}}`, so Codex does not read Claude's `hooks/hooks.json` and warn.
- **Real shim files.** The shims are real copies, not symlinks. The new `test_codex_markers_shims_match` checks that they match `plugins/worktrunk/hooks/` byte for byte, that the directory holds only those three files, and that the manifest has no `version`. Neither manifest has a `version` today, and no release step edits `plugin.json`.
- **Uninstall.** `uninstall` removes the markers plugin first. `codex plugin remove` already exits 0 for a plugin that isn't installed, so older single-plugin installs uninstall cleanly.

Verification: the Codex plugin, layout, help and docs-sync tests pass locally, with snapshots updated for the new install and uninstall output. In the sandbox, the full `pre-merge` gate stopped on `cargo fmt` (fixed in this commit) and on test failures that come from the sandbox itself: blocked Unix sockets, a `0644` signing key, and a nushell autoload file left in the shared home. `test_config_show_codex_available` fails the same way on `main` here. Two things are unverified. I haven't run a real Codex session against this branch. I also haven't checked that running `wt config plugins codex install` again succeeds when the marketplace is already registered, which is why the upgrade note in the docs names the direct `codex plugin add` command.

Closes #4654

+rem avoids cmd's initial-quote stripping; /d disables AutoRun for this cmd hop.
+rem The outer cmd, if Codex uses one, still runs its own AutoRun. A cmd-session
+rem lookup of the bare `cmd` can also resolve an executable in the project cwd.

+set "GIT_RUNTIME=%GIT_RUNTIME:/=\%"

+goto :eof
+
+:accept

+goto :eof

+# Cross-platform wrapper for the worktrunk CLI.
+# If WORKTRUNK_BIN is set, uses that path exclusively.
+# Otherwise, on Windows (MSYS/Cygwin), prefers git-wt.exe over wt and
+# rejects wt if it resolves to Windows Terminal (.../WindowsApps/wt.exe).
+# On other platforms, uses wt directly.
+# Usage: wt.sh [args...]

+# environment -- so an inherited WT would be what the final check accepts and
+# runs, Windows Terminal included.
+WT=""
+

+    if ! command -v "$WORKTRUNK_BIN" >/dev/null 2>&1; then

+        exit 1

+elif [[ "$(uname -o 2>/dev/null)" =~ ^(Msys|Cygwin)$ ]]; then

+        fi
+
+        WT=wt
+    fi
+else
+    # non-Windows, always use wt
+    WT=wt
+fi
+
+if [[ -z "$WT" ]] || ! command -v "$WT" >/dev/null 2>&1; then

title: fix(switch): clear a stale marker when --create makes the branch
body:
A branch deleted outside `wt` (for example with `git branch -D`) leaves its `worktrunk.state.<branch>.marker` key in git config. A later `wt switch --create` with the same name then showed the old 🤖/💬. Now `wt switch --create` clears that branch's marker once `git worktree add -b` succeeds. #4684 already clears the marker on every `wt` deletion path. This is the follow-up the maintainer asked for when closing #4685.

- The deletion helper from #4684 moves to `Repository::clear_branch_marker`, and both call sites use it. It is still best effort: a failed unset is logged at debug level, and only marker JSON is removed, so a `vars` entry named `marker` that shares the key is left alone.
- Only `--create` clears the marker. Switching to an existing branch keeps its marker, and so does a DWIM checkout from a remote branch or a PR/MR ref.
- A branch deleted and recreated with plain `git` still keeps its marker until `wt config state marker clear`. The marker help, its generated docs, and the help snapshot now say so.

`test_switch_create_clears_stale_marker` sets a marker on a branch name that has no branch and on an existing branch. It then runs `wt switch --create` for the first and plain `wt switch` for the second. It fails without the change, because the stale marker survives, and passes with it. The existing `deletion_*` unit tests pass on the moved helper.

Refs #4683

title: fix(plugins): skip Windows Terminal's wt in the pi, omp, and OpenCode plugins
body:
The pi, oh-my-pi, and OpenCode plugins ran a bare `wt`. On Windows that name usually resolves to Windows Terminal's app-execution alias in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\WindowsApps`. The alias exits 0 and reports the unknown program in a popup, so every activity-marker update opened an error window. OpenCode's worktree `switch`/`remove` strategy also never reached worktrunk. The Claude Code and Codex hooks didn't have this problem because they run through `plugins/worktrunk/hooks/wt.sh`, which already handles this case.

Each plugin now has a small `worktrunkBin()` that follows `wt.sh`'s policy: use `WORKTRUNK_BIN` if set, otherwise use `wt` off Windows. On Windows, it walks `PATH` in order and prefers `git-wt.exe`, then accepts a `wt.exe` only if the first one found isn't under `WindowsApps`. When nothing usable is found, marker updates are skipped, and OpenCode's strategy throws an error naming `git-wt.exe` and `WORKTRUNK_BIN`. The helper is copied into all three files because each one is installed as a standalone file.

Verification: dev/*.ts has no test harness, so I checked locally with Node 22's type stripping. The check fakes `process.platform = "win32"`, builds a `PATH` with a `WindowsApps/wt.exe` ahead of a real `wt.exe`, and stubs `pi.exec`. Before this change, both the pi and omp plugins exec `wt` (the Terminal alias). After it, they skip; they pick `git-wt.exe` when it's present and `wt` when the real binary comes first on `PATH`. OpenCode's strategy surfaces the new error. The existing plugin install/config integration tests pass.

**Not verified on Windows:** I couldn't run a real Windows host. `lstat` is used instead of `exists` so the alias's reparse point still counts as present, which keeps the search order the same as Windows' own lookup. It's worth a check on a Windows machine with the Terminal alias enabled.

The issue's other suggestion is still open: warning when a `wt` on PATH turns out not to be worktrunk. That needs a choice about where a plugin should report it, so it's not in this PR.

Closes #4697 — automated triage

title: fix(list): probe both IPv4 and IPv6 loopback for the URL health check
body:
## Problem

The URL health check only probed `127.0.0.1`. A dev server bound only to `::1` — Vite's default `localhost` on macOS — is reachable but shown as inactive.

## Fix

Probe both loopback families (`127.0.0.1` and `::1`) for the port parsed by `parse_port_from_url`, using the matching socket domain. Any success counts as active. This is a local default assumption; the check never resolves DNS or contacts a remote host.

`parse_port_from_url` is unchanged — no host parsing, IPv6 literals, userinfo, or scheme-less handling.

## Tests

Added a unit test that binds `127.0.0.1` and `[::1]` listeners and asserts the URL status is active for each, exercising both socket-domain branches.

title: fix(tests): seed tempfile's name generator per process
body:
On Windows CI, temp entries under `D:\tmp` failed with `Access is denied` because concurrent test processes were generating the same names. `tempfile` takes its names from `fastrand`, and fastrand seeds its thread-local generator only from `Instant::now()` and the thread id (smol-rs/fastrand#130). Under nextest each test is a separate process whose thread ids start from the same values, so two processes that seed in the same clock tick generate the same names. If the duplicate name is held by a live entry, `tempfile` gets `AlreadyExists` and retries. If another process has just deleted that entry, Windows returns `PermissionDenied` (os error 5), which `tempfile` passes to the caller. That is the failure in #3613, #3619 and the `TempDir::new()` panic in #4692.

The suite's temp helpers now reseed that generator per process:

- `worktrunk::testing::tempdir()` and `named_tempfile()` replace `tempfile::tempdir()`, `TempDir::new()` and `NamedTempFile::new()` at every test call site, including `wt-perf`. `test_tempdir()` and the fixture-template scratch directory go through the same builder. On a thread's first use, the builder calls `fastrand::seed` with a value from `RandomState::new()`, which std keys from OS randomness, so the seed differs between processes even when the clock reading matches. A probe confirmed that seeding fastrand fixes the next tempfile name, so both crates share the one generator. Names keep tempfile's `.tmpXXXXXX` length, which matters because a pid prefix pushed the macOS fsmonitor socket path past `sun_path`.
- A new root `clippy.toml` uses `disallowed-methods` to reject those three constructors in new code. The one production caller, `format_migration_diff`, keeps `tempfile::tempdir()` with a call-site `#[expect]`.
- `fastrand` becomes a direct dependency. It resolves to the same 2.5.0 that `tempfile` already uses.

<details><summary>Windows reproduction</summary>

I ran a temporary workflow on `windows-2025` with `TMP=D:\tmp`, set up the way `ci.yaml` does it. Batches of short-lived processes each created `TempDir`s and `NamedTempFile`s with `tempfile` 3.27.0 and fastrand 2.5.0, and the parent recorded every name and error:

| processes × parallel × per-process | names created more than once | `Access is denied` |
|---|---|---|
| 3000 × 16 × 5 | 86 / 30,000 | 5 |
| 3000 × 64 × 5 | 49 / 30,000 | 8 |
| 400 × 16 × 200 | 763 / 160,000 | 14 |

All 27 denials hit a name that another process had also generated. The same program on Linux generated no duplicates in 30,000 names.

This PR doesn't rerun that experiment against the new helpers either. The Windows `test` leg on this PR is the check, and the recurrence rate (#3619 measured 4 failures in 80 loop runs) means one green leg is weak evidence.

</details>

Locally, clippy is clean across the workspace, and the lib tests covering the directive helpers, `cache::` and the template claim pass. An earlier full `cargo nextest run --all-features` of the pid-prefix version passed 547

title: fix(alias): show project aliases with retired template variables migrated
body:
`wt config alias show` now displays project aliases with retired template variables rewritten, matching what the alias actually runs. Previously a project alias written as `code {{ repo_root }}` showed `{{ repo_root }}`, while execution (via `ProjectConfig::load`) ran the migrated `{{ repo_path }}` — and user aliases, loaded through `UserConfig::load`, already showed migrated text, so the two sources disagreed in one listing.

The cause was `load_project_aliases_silent` parsing `.config/wt.toml` with a bare `toml::from_str`, on the stated premise that the `aliases` table has no deprecated forms. The first `DEPRECATION_RULES` row (`migrate_template_vars_doc`) rewrites retired variables in every string value, aliases included. The fix runs the file through the same silent `migrate_content` that `wt config show` and the user-config loader use before deserializing, and corrects that docstring. The same listing feeds the `Aliases:` section of `wt --help`, which shows names only, so only `show` changes visibly.

`test_config_alias_show_migrates_retired_template_vars` configures a project alias with `{{ repo_root }}` and a user alias with `{{ worktree }}`; before the fix its snapshot showed `repo_root` for the project entry, now both show their replacements.

title: docs(reference): repair broken in-page anchors for custom columns and default_branch object
body:
## What

Nine in-page anchor links in the reference docs point at fragments that no heading generates:

- `](#custom-columns)` - the heading is `### Custom columns [experimental]` (`skills/worktrunk/reference/list.md:123`, `#### Custom columns [experimental]` at `skills/worktrunk/reference/config.md:231`), so the generated fragment is `#custom-columns-experimental`. 6 links updated (list.md x2, config.md x1, plus the `plugins/worktrunk/` synced copies).
- `](#default-branch-object)` - the heading is `### default_branch object` (`skills/worktrunk/reference/list.md:331`, `docs/src/content/docs/list.md:347`), so the fragment is `#default_branch-object` (underscore, not hyphen). 3 links updated (skills + plugins list.md, docs list.md).

The `docs/src/content/docs/list.md` copy of the custom-columns links was left alone: its own heading is `### Custom columns` (no `[experimental]` suffix), so `#custom-columns` resolves there.

## Why

Readers of the Columns table and the JSON object docs click these links and land nowhere. The default_branch link is especially easy to miss since `head-object` / `worktree-object` next to it do resolve.

## How it was verified

- The `skills/worktrunk/reference/` and `plugins/worktrunk/skills/worktrunk/reference/` copies were kept byte-identical.

## Follow-ups deliberately left out

- The `[experimental]` suffix in the headings leaks into the fragments; renaming headings would produce cleaner anchors but changes existing inbound links elsewhere, so only the links were repaired.

+static IN_PAGE_LINK_PATTERN: LazyLock<Regex> =
+    LazyLock::new(|| Regex::new(r"\]\(#([^)\s]+)\)").unwrap());
+
+/// Anchor GitHub's slugger generates for a heading: lowercase, drop
+/// punctuation except `-` and `_`, spaces to hyphens.
+fn github_heading_anchor(heading: &str) -> String {
+    heading
+        .to_lowercase()
+        .chars()
+        .filter_map(|c| match c {
+            ' ' => Some('-'),
+            c if c.is_alphanumeric() || c == '-' || c == '_' => Some(c),
+            _ => None,
+        })
+        .collect()
+}
+
+/// Rewrite in-page fragments from the site's heading slug to GitHub's.
+///
+/// Help text links headings by their worktrunk.dev id, where `slugHeading`
+/// turns `_` into `-` and the `[experimental]` badge contributes no text.
+/// Skill files render with GitHub's slugger, which keeps `_` and the literal
+/// `[experimental]` suffix, so those links would otherwise land nowhere.
+fn rewrite_fragments_for_github(content: &str) -> String {
+    let mut site_to_github: BTreeMap<String, String> = BTreeMap::new();
+    let mut in_code_block = false;
+    for line in content.lines() {
+        if line.trim_start().starts_with("```") {
+            in_code_block = !in_code_block;
+            continue;
+        }
+        if in_code_block {
+            continue;
+        }
+        let Some(text) = line
+            .strip_prefix('#')
+            .map(|rest| rest.trim_start_matches('#'))
+            .and_then(|rest| rest.strip_prefix(' '))
+        else {
+            continue;
+        };
+        let site = heading_to_anchor(&text.replace("[experimental]", ""));
+        site_to_github
+            .entry(site)
+            .or_insert_with(|| github_heading_anchor(text.trim()));
+    }
+
+    IN_PAGE_LINK_PATTERN
+        .replace_all(content, |caps: &regex::Captures| {
+            let fragment = &caps[1];
+            let target = site_to_github
+                .get(fragment)
+                .map_or(fragment, String::as_str);
+            format!("](#{target})")
+        })
+        .into_owned()
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn test_skill_fragments_follow_github_slugs() {
+    let content = r"See [custom columns](#custom-columns), [default_branch](#default-branch-object), and [CI](#ci-status).
+
+### Custom columns [experimental]
+
+### default_branch object
+
+### CI status
+";
+    let rewritten = rewrite_fragments_for_github(content);
+    assert!(rewritten.contains("[custom columns](#custom-columns-experimental)"));
+    assert!(rewritten.contains("[default_branch](#default_branch-object)"));
+    assert!(rewritten.contains("[CI](#ci-status)"));
+}

title: fix(remove): clear a branch's marker when wt deletes the branch
body:
`wt` deleted branches but left `worktrunk.state.<branch>.marker` in git config, so a later branch with the same name came up in `wt list` with the old 🤖/💬. Every `wt` deletion path goes through `delete_branch_if_safe`: `wt remove` (foreground and the detached background child), `wt merge`, the picker, and branch-only removal. That function now unsets the branch's marker after a forced or integrated deletion. A branch that is kept (unmerged, checked out elsewhere, or moved by a race) keeps its marker. Unsetting is best effort: the branch is already gone by then, so a failure gets a debug log line and does not fail the removal.

`deletion_clears_branch_marker` covers the integrated, forced, and kept cases. It fails without the change and passes with it. I also ran the issue's repro through `wt remove --yes feature` (the default background path). Before the change the marker key survived; after it no `worktrunk.state.*` keys were left. The marker help and the FAQ's branch-deletion section now say this.

This PR does not cover:
- **`vars` entries**: `worktrunk.state.<branch>.vars.*` entries also outlive the branch. They are user data rather than activity status, so whether branch deletion should drop them is a maintainer call.
- **Branches deleted outside `wt`**: a branch deleted with plain `git branch -D`, as in the issue's repro, still leaves its marker. The issue suggests either having `wt list` ignore markers for missing branches or adding a `wt config state prune`; both are product decisions.

Refs #4683 — automated triage

title: fix(list): measure truncated cells by grapheme cluster so VS16 emoji don't overflow
body:
`truncate_visible` summed per-`char` widths, so a VS16 emoji presentation sequence such as `♻️` (`U+267B U+FE0F`) measured 1 + 0 = 1 cell, while the terminal and the rest of the layout (`UnicodeWidthStr::width`) count it as 2. A truncated Message cell starting with one came out one cell wider than its column, which wraps the row in `wt list | cat` and throws off the progressive renderer's cursor math. The loop now walks grapheme clusters and measures each with the string width, so the kept prefix agrees with every other width measure and a cut can no longer split a base character from its selector.

`unicode-segmentation` 1.12 was already in `Cargo.lock` transitively; this adds it as a direct dependency.

The new assertions in `test_truncate_visible` fail on the old loop (`"♻️ refactor:…"`, 13 cells for a 12-cell budget) and pass now. Running the issue's repro at `COLUMNS=100` against the fixed build, both Message cells (`✨ feat: ad…` and `♻️ refactor…`) are 12 cells.

Closes #4681 — automated triage
author: worktrunk-bot

title: fix(shell): treat PowerShell directive paths literally
body:
When the PowerShell temporary directory contains wildcard characters such as `temp[1]`, `wt switch` can finish without changing the parent shell's directory. The directive file is written, but the wrapper treats its path as a wildcard during lookup and cleanup, leaving the file behind.

Use `-LiteralPath` for all four directive-file operations. Add a regression that checks both the directory change and removal of the temporary file, and refresh the generated PowerShell snapshot.

Validation: all 4 PowerShell integration tests pass with all features enabled, including the new regression. The shell-generation snapshot test, pre-commit checks (including clippy), doctests and rustdoc also pass. The original template reproduced the failure on Windows PowerShell 5; the corrected template switches directories and leaves no directive file on both Windows PowerShell 5 and PowerShell 7.6.9.

The full `hook pre-merge --yes` gate did not pass on this Windows host: 4,693 passed, 74 failed, 40 skipped. Failures include configuration/statusline snapshots, switch tests and the performance helper CLI; those failures and snapshots are outside this change and were not accepted or modified.

title: test: format fork remote URLs without spawning gh or glab
body:
`git::remote_ref::github::tests::test_fork_remote_url_formats` ran the real `gh config get git_protocol --host …` from the test runner's PATH, and on Windows CI that subprocess has twice hung past nextest's 180s limit (#4577, #4672) while every other test passed. The test only checked the URL shape, accepting either protocol, so it never needed `gh`. URL formatting now lives in a pure `host_remote_url(host, owner, repo, ssh)` helper in `src/git/remote_ref/mod.rs`. Its unit test pins both the SSH and HTTPS forms and spawns nothing. The GitLab test had the same structure with `glab`, so it moves to the shared helper too.

`fork_remote_url` behaves the same for both forges. The protocol query is still exercised end to end by the mock-CLI integration tests in `tests/integration_tests/switch.rs`, which answer `config get git_protocol` with `ssh` and assert the `--host` argument for GitHub and GitLab.

This change does not explain why `gh` stalled on the Windows runner; neither timeout log shows anything from inside the subprocess. It removes the test's dependency on the runner's `gh`, which was the only thing exposing the stall.

Closes #4672 — automated triage

title: fix(docs): stop move-changes after stash failures
body:
The documented `move-changes` alias now stops when either stash operation fails. A failed stash push no longer starts the new worktree, and a failed stash pop no longer runs the forwarded command in a partially restored worktree.

The docs sync test and site build passed. A shell reproduction confirmed that the previous command ran its follow-up after a failed stash pop and the revised command exits with that failure. The full pre-merge gate ran 5,476 tests: 5,469 passed, seven failed in local environment-sensitive tests (including unavailable Unix sockets, shell snapshots, and signing key permissions). This is a documentation-only edit, so the shell reproduction covers the changed recipe; PR CI will verify the published revision.

title: fix(picker): flash success feedback after alt-x removes worktree
body:
Fixes #4636 

When using `alt-x` to remove a worktree but keep its unmerged branch, the picker optimistically morphs the row. Previously, if the background removal succeeded, it didn't provide any visual feedback to confirm the action (unlike the failure paths).

This updates the background thread to flash a transient success message (`Removed <branch> worktree; kept branch`) in the header once it confirms the worktree directory is actually gone. 

Also updated `test_apply_morphs_unmerged_worktree_to_branch_row` to wait for and assert this new header flash.
author: Yash2031v

title: Retry failed plugin worktree lookups instead of caching misses
body:
Calling /wt-diff before git init caches a null worktree lookup for the session directory. Initializing the repository afterward does not help: subsequent commands reuse that miss and report no Git worktree for the rest of the module lifetime. A transient Git/process failure is similarly cached permanently.

Cache only successful locate results. Successful worktree lookups still avoid repeated Git subprocesses. This intentionally trades negative-cache savings for recovery: three repeated non-repository lookups now perform three Git probes rather than one. These probes occur when locating for the command/open pane; passive hooks still only note directories. Positive-cache invalidation behavior is unchanged.

Added a canonical Claude test for a failed command followed by a now-available repository, opening the pane and retaining the successful lookup cache.

Native plugin validation at `1e4d728a2c740b93c945c3f6a76cbde2c77899d5` with Claude Code 2.1.316: `claude plugin validate plugins/worktrunk` passes with the existing missing-version warning, and `claude plugin test plugins/worktrunk` passes all 9 canonical tests. Restoring only the relevant production file to upstream while retaining the new canonical test gives 8 passes and 1 failure; the unchanged upstream suite passes all 8 tests. The plugin snapshots were checked against every tracked Git blob at the PR head. These local runs use the canonical mocked host events, not a live terminal/provider session.

Additional Git-boundary evidence: Node 24 executes the actual locate function body extracted from register.tsx, with TypeScript types stripped, against real temporary Git repositories. Four checks cover git init after a miss, a controlled transient process failure followed by actual Git discovery, successful-cache reuse, and repeated non-repository probe counts. Unchanged source: two failures/two passes. Fixed: four passes in 490ms. That standalone runner checks the Git boundary separately from the native plugin suite; no live-session or maintainer acceptance is claimed.

AI disclosure: implementation, tests and description were prepared with Codex and independently reviewed by another Codex agent. No human-authorship or human-review claim is made.
author: rudycelekli

title: fix(list): deduplicate concurrent ahead/behind counts
body:
Two statusline tasks can request the same ahead/behind SHA pair concurrently when local `main` trails `origin/main`. Each previously missed the persistent cache and launched its own `git rev-list --count`. A per-repository, per-pair in-memory cache now holds the first computation while the other caller waits; the persistent cache still serves later processes.

The new statusline regression test reproduced two matching `rev-list` calls before the change and passes with at most one after it. `cargo test --lib test_ahead_behind_reads_cache`, the focused integration test, and `cargo fmt --check` pass.

Closes #4662 — automated triage

title: chore: bump jdx/packslip from 1.11.1 to 1.11.2
body:
Bumps [jdx/packslip](https://github.com/jdx/packslip) from 1.11.1 to 1.11.2.
Release notes

Sourced from jdx/packslip's releases.

v1.11.2: Detect replaced public keys that reuse the old key ID

packslip install now asks for approval when a key-signed project switches to a different public key that keeps the old key ID. This release also puts limits on how much work a hostile bundle can force the verifiers to do, and fixes two argument-handling gaps in the GitHub Actions. The format and specification are unchanged.

Fixed

  • packslip install treats a replacement public key with the same key ID as a trust change. A minisign key ID is eight bytes of text in the public key file. It is not derived from the key itself. Before this release, the continuity check compared only that ID, so a different key with the old ID was accepted through --pubkey or pins.d without approval, and install then remembered the new key. Each key-signed record now also stores a fingerprint of the whole public key. A changed key is reported as public key changed from <old> to <new> and needs --accept-trust-change=<id> like any other trust change. That means one approval for the release list and one for the release, as the trust guide already described. Records for keyless projects are unchanged. (#305, @​jdx)
    • Existing histories: On the first install after you upgrade, records without a fingerprint are filled in from the public key the history already remembers, so that install catches a same-ID replacement. If a history has a key-signed record but no remembered key, it adopts the first key it sees, as before. If an earlier version already accepted a same-ID replacement for the release list, the old key is lost and cannot be recovered. In that case the release check uses the replacement key as its baseline and does not catch the swap. Older packslip versions ignore the new field.
    • Pending approvals: If a key change was waiting for approval when you upgraded, its approval ID changes. Approve it again with the new ID.
  • Verifiers reject oversized or malformed bundle data before doing expensive work. (#304, @​jdx)
    • The standalone verifier (verifier/packslip-verify.mjs) rejects inclusion proofs whose logIndex or treeSize is not a non-negative int64. Before, a very long digit string took time

Bumps [rstest](https://github.com/la10736/rstest) from 0.27.0 to 0.28.0.
Release notes

Sourced from rstest's releases.

v0.28.0

[0.28.0] 2026/10/18

Changed

  • #[case(...)] argument attributes other than #[case(opt)], #[case(default)] and #[case(default(...))] are now rejected: before they were silently accepted as #[case]. #[case()] is still accepted as #[case].
  • rstest_reuse 0.7.1: when the function where the template is applied defines a #[case(...)] argument modifier, it replaces the template's #[case] attribute.

Added

  • Cases can omit the values of #[case(default)], #[case(default(expr))] and #[case(opt)] arguments: the trailing values can be omitted and _ can be used to skip a value. #[case(opt)] wraps the given value in Some() and uses None when omitted. Magic conversion works for #[case(default(expr))] expressions and #[case(opt)] values. See #325 and #327, thanks to @​Atreyagaurav.
Changelog

Sourced from rstest's changelog.

[0.28.0] 2026/10/18

  • #[case(...)] argument attributes other than #[case(opt)], #[case(default)] and #[case(default(...))] are now rejected: before they were silently accepted as #[case]. #[case()] is still accepted as #[case].
  • rstest_reuse 0.7.1: when the function where the template is applied defines a #[case(...)] argument modifier, it replaces the template's #[case] attribute.

Added

  • Cases can omit the values of #[case(default)], #[case(default(expr))] and #[case(opt)] arguments: the trailing values can be omitted and _ can be used to skip a value. #[case(opt)] wraps the given value in Some() and uses None when omitted. Magic conversion works for #[case(default(expr))] expressions and #[case(opt)] values. See #325 and #327, thanks to @​Atreyagaurav

title: chore: bump jsonschema from 0.58.4 to 0.60.2
body:
Bumps [jsonschema](https://github.com/Stranger6667/jsonschema) from 0.58.4 to 0.60.2.
Release notes

Sourced from jsonschema's releases.

[Rust] Release 0.60.2

Fixed

  • Stack overflow when building validators for unevaluated* schemas with $ref cycles across $id resources.

[Ruby] Release 0.60.2

Fixed

  • Stack overflow when building validators for unevaluated* schemas with $ref cycles across $id resources.

[Python] Release 0.60.1

Fixed

  • Wrong results in type: integer, const, enum, uniqueItems, multipleOf, minimum, maximum, exclusiveMinimum and exclusiveMaximum for numbers with exponents past one million, such as 1e-2000000.

Performance

  • Validation of numbers with many digits or large exponents in const, enum, uniqueItems, type: integer, multipleOf, minimum, maximum, exclusiveMinimum and exclusiveMaximum taking time growing faster than the square of the digit count, instead of at most the square.
  • Validation of numbers with more than ten thousand digits, written or implied by their exponent, taking time linear in their written length instead of quadratic in their digit count.

[Rust] Release 0.60.1

  • Panic on numbers past f64 in const, enum, minimum, maximum, exclusiveMinimum, exclusiveMaximum and type: integer when another crate in the build enables serde_json/arbitrary_precision while the arbitrary-precision feature is off. #1790
  • #[jsonschema::validator] panicking during expansion, or generating code that panics, on schema numbers past f64 when another crate in the build enables serde_json/arbitrary_precision while the arbitrary-precision feature is off. Such numbers are compile errors, as without that serde_json feature. #1790
  • const, enum and uniqueItems treating objects with the same members in a different key order as unequal when another crate in the build enables serde_json/preserve_order. #1791
  • Wrong results in type: integer, const

Bumps the patch group with 5 updates: | Package | From | To | | --- | --- | --- | | [minijinja](https://github.com/mitsuhiko/minijinja) | `3.0.2` | `3.0.5` | | [unicode-width](https://github.com/unicode-rs/unicode-width) | `0.2.2` | `0.2.3` | | [ignore](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep) | `0.4.33` | `0.4.34` | | [rustix](https://github.com/bytecodealliance/rustix) | `1.1.5` | `1.1.6` | | [similar](https://github.com/mitsuhiko/similar) | `3.2.0` | `3.2.1` | Updates `minijinja` from 3.0.2 to 3.0.5
Changelog

Sourced from minijinja's changelog.

3.0.5

  • Fixed a panic or abort in Rust when buffering an iterator that reports a huge size hint, or when passing a huge count to the batch or slice filters. Filters like list, sort, reverse, map, slice and batch as well as slicing and concatenating sequences now cap how much they preallocate, so [1, 2]|batch(4611686018427387904) is [[1, 2]] instead of failing with "capacity overflow". #483
  • Fixed floats in Go switching to exponent notation from one million up, so 1234567.5 printed as 1.2345675e+06. Like in Rust, a float now prints as its shortest exact decimal without an exponent, so 1234567.5 is 1234567.5 and 1e20 is 100000000000000000000.0. Inside lists and maps, exponent notation is only used below 1e-4 and from 1e16 up, written like 1e20 and 1e-5. NaN now prints as NaN, and infinity inside a list as inf instead of +Inf. #984
  • Fixed %s in the format filter formatting floats with %g rules, so "%s"|format(1234567.5) was 1.23457e+06. Like in Python, floats are now formatted like str() does: 1234567.5, 1e+16, 1e-05 or nan. The 0, + and space flags are ignored for floats and strings with %s, like in Python. This applies to both Rust and Go. #984
  • Fixed the tojson filter in Go writing floats like integers. Like in Rust, a float stays a float in the output, so 1.0|tojson is 1.0 instead of 1, large and small magnitudes use exponent notation (1.5e+16, 2.5e-7) and infinity becomes null instead of an error. The same applies to values rendered wit

title: Add a /wt-diff pane to the Claude Code plugin
body:
The Claude Code plugin gains `/wt-diff`, a pane beside the conversation that lists the worktrees the session has worked in, with the selected one's `wt step diff` below it, drawn file by file with Claude Code's own diff renderer. It is a hooks module, Claude Code's early-access function hooks API, and the plugin's only one.

A worktree joins the list when the session starts or moves into it, or when the session or a subagent edits a file there or runs a Bash command there that isn't read-only. Until `/wt-diff` first runs, the hooks only note those directories in session state: no `git` or `wt` process runs and nothing is drawn, which a test asserts. While the pane is open, `wt list --format=json` (once per repository) supplies the rows and `wt step diff` the selected worktree's files; it refreshes on open, on selection, after a burst of non-read-only tool calls goes quiet, and at the end of each turn.

Keys: `1`–`9` select a worktree, `j`/`k` move between files (`ctrl+↓`/`ctrl+↑` from the prompt, borrowing the chords of Claude Code's own diff panel), `r` refreshes, and the arrows and page keys scroll. Running `/wt-diff` again, or `ctrl+x tab`, gives the pane the keyboard back. A plugin can't ship keybindings, so the pane has no dedicated chord.

Compatibility: Claude Code releases without hooks modules drop the `modules` key and still load the command hooks (checked on 2.1.100), so the 🤖/💬 markers keep working there. Codex and Gemini never read the module.

Where to look:

- `plugins/worktrunk/hooks/register.tsx` — the module, with its spec at the top.
- `plugins/worktrunk/hooks/patch.ts` — splits the patch into files, with rename and mode notes.
- `plugins/worktrunk/types/index.d.ts` — the state contract; `tests/diff.test.tsx` — the suite.
- `hooks/hooks.json` gains `modules`, `plugin.json` gains `types`, and the agent integration docs gain a `/wt-diff` section (skills mirrors regenerated).

One drawing holds 100,000 characters, so the selected file always draws (cut at whole hunks, or to the start of its first hunk, if it must be) and the others draw within the remaining budget; a patch over the 4 MiB that `$.process.run` captures drops its last file and says so.

Checked locally: `claude plugin validate plugins/worktrunk`, `claude plugin test plugins/worktrunk` (8 pass), `test_docs_are_in_sync` and `test_plugin_layout_is_consolidated`, and live sessions on Claude Code 2.1.314.

> _This was written by Claude Code on behalf of max-sixty_

This plugin provides configuration guidance (LLM commit messages, project hooks, worktree paths) and automatic activity tracking (🤖/💬 indicators in `wt list` showing active Claude sessions).",

This plugin provides configuration guidance (LLM commit messages, project hooks, worktree paths), automatic activity tracking (🤖/💬 indicators in `wt list` showing active Claude sessions), and a `/wt-diff` pane showing each worktree's changes.",

Worktree isolation needs worktree-lifecycle hooks, which only Claude Code and OpenCode 2 expose, so Codex, Pi, oh-my-pi, and Gemini users invoke `wt switch --create` and `wt remove` directly.

The plugin's `PermissionRequest` hook answers yes for a worktree of the repository the session is working in that sits where `worktree-path` puts its branch, so a background session doesn't stop at that prompt. Entering any other worktree still asks.
 
+## `/wt-diff` pane (Claude Code only)
+
+`/wt-diff` opens a pane beside the conversation that lists the worktrees the session has worked in, with the selected one's [`wt step diff`](/step/#wt-step-diff) below: everything since the branch left the default branch, committed, uncommitted, and untracked. `/wt-diff <branch>` selects another worktree.
+

+

+|---|---|
+| `1`–`9` | Select a worktree |
+| `j` / `k` | Next or previous file |
+| `ctrl+↓` / `ctrl+↑` | Next or previous file, from the prompt |
+| `r` | Refresh |
+| ↑ ↓, PageUp, PageDown | Scroll |
+
+The other keys work while the pane has the keyboard, which it takes when it opens. Running `/wt-diff` again gives it back, as does `ctrl+x tab`, which moves focus from the prompt to the line above it when another plugin draws one, then to the pane. `esc` returns to the prompt.
+
+The pane needs a Claude Code release that loads plugin hooks modules; earlier releases load the rest of the plugin without it.
+
 ## Statusline (Claude Code only)
 
 `wt list statusline --format=claude-code` outputs a single-line status for the Claude Code statusline. Claude Code runs it in the background, which is what makes the occasional 1–2 second CI fetch invisible.

--- plugins/worktrunk/hooks/patch.ts (+117/-0)
@@ -0,0 +1,117 @@
+import type { FileDiff } from '../types'
+
+/**
+ * Splits a `git diff` patch into its files, keeping each file's hunks as the
+ * source a `Code` element draws under `format: 'diff'`.
+ *
+ * Reads the headers git writes with `--no-color --no-ext-diff`, the `a/` and
+ * `b/` prefixes and `core.quotePath=false`: `diff --git a/<old> b/<new>`, then
+ * `new file`, `deleted file`, `rename to`, `Binary files` or `---`/`+++`
+ * lines, then hunks. Git ends a `---`/`+++` name holding a space with a tab,
+ * and still C-quotes one holding a tab, newline, quote or backslash.
+ */
+export function parsePatch(patch: string): FileDiff[] {
+  const files: FileDiff[] = []
+  for (const chunk of patch.split(/^(?=diff --git )/m)) {
+    if (!chunk.startsWith('diff --git ')) {
+      continue
+    }
+    const lines = chunk.split('\n')
+    const first = lines[0] ?? ''
+    const hunkAt = lines.findIndex(line => line.startsWith('@@'))
+    const header = hunkAt === -1 ? lines : lines.slice(0, hunkAt)
+    const body = hunkAt === -1 ? [] : lines.slice(hunkAt)
+    const named = (prefix: string) => {
+      const rest = header.find(line => line.startsWith(prefix))?.slice(prefix.length)
+      return rest === undefined ? undefined : unquote(rest)
+    }
+    // A `---` or `+++` name without its side's prefix; `/dev/null` has none.
+    const side = (prefix: string, at: string) => {
+      const name = named(prefix)
+      return name?.startsWith(at) === true ? name.slice(at.length) : undefined
+    }
+    const has = (prefix: string) => header.some(line => line.startsWith(prefix))
+
+    // `+++ b/<path>` names the file after the change; a deletion has
+    // `+++ /dev/null` and names it on `---`. A file with no hunks (binary,
+    // mode-only, pure rename) names it only on `diff --git`.
+    const quoted = / ("(?:[^"\\]|\\.)*")$/.exec(first)?.[1]
+    const path =
+      named('rename to ') ??
+      side('+++ ', 'b/') ??
+      side('--- ', 'a/') ??

+        ? first.replace(/^diff --git a\/.* b\//, '')
+        : unquote(quoted).replace(/^b\//, ''))

+    let deleted = 0

+      if (line.startsWith('+')) {
+        added += 1
+      } else if (line.startsWith('-')) {
+        deleted += 1
+      }
+    }
+
+    const status: FileDiff['status'] = has('Binary files ')
+      ? 'binary'
+      : has('new file mode')
+        ? 'added'
+        : has('deleted file mode')

+          : has('rename to ')
+            ? 'renamed'
+            : 'modified'
+
+    const from = named('rename from ')
+    const modes = [named('old mode '), named('new mode ')]
+    const notes = [
+      from === undefined ? null : `from ${from}`,
+      modes[0] === undefined ? null : `mode ${modes[0]} → ${modes[1]}`,
+    ].filter(note => note !== null)
+
+    files.push({
+      path: printable(path),
+      status,
+      added,
+      deleted,
+      note: notes.length === 0 ? null : printable(notes.join(', ')),
+      hunks: printable(body.join('\n').replace(/\n+$/, '')),
+    })
+  }
+  return files
+}
+
+const ESCAPES: Record<string, string> = {
+  a: String.fromCharCode(7),
+  b: '\b',
+  f: '\f',
+  n: '\n',
+  r: '\r',
+  t: '\t',
+  v: '\v',
+}

+/**

+ * ended with a tab when it holds a space.
+ */
+function unquote(name: string): string {
+  if (!name.startsWith('"')) {
+    return name.replace(/\t$/, '')
+  }
+  return name
+    .slice(1, name.lastIndexOf('"'))
+    .replace(/\\([0-7]{3}|.)/g, (_, code: string) =>
+      code.length === 3 ? String.fromCharCode(Number.parseInt(code, 8)) : (ESCAPES[code] ?? code),
+    )
+}

title: fix(remove): find Linux reap candidates through procfs
body:
On Linux, `wt remove --reap` now reads process working directories from `/proc` instead of waiting for a system-wide `lsof` scan. A slow `lsof` probe could exceed the five-second timeout and silently leave a detached worktree process running. The existing terminal and self exclusions remain in the reap path; other Unix platforms continue using `lsof`.

The regression test forces `lsof` to return no cwd records while a detached process is running. It failed before this change with “No processes to reap” and passes with procfs discovery. The reap unit tests and three reap integration tests pass.

Closes #4630 — automated triage
author: worktrunk-bot

title: fix(tether): stop supervised processes on Ctrl-C
body:
`wt step tether` put the supervised command in a separate process group, but Ctrl-C reached only the supervisor. The supervisor exited before its cleanup sweep, leaving the command running. This PR keeps a foreground signal lease while tether waits and has the reaper terminate the supervised group when the command is interrupted.

The integration test sends SIGINT to the supervisor's group and verifies that the supervised group exits. It failed before the production change and now passes. All four tether integration tests pass locally; CI will check the platform matrix.

Fixes #4622.
author: worktrunk-bot

title: test(remove): wait for staged trash cleanup after inherited lock
body:
The `feature-powerset` check on #4597 failed because `background_removal_preserves_native_path_arguments` expected staged trash to be empty immediately after removal. A concurrently forked child can briefly inherit the trash drain lock, so the test's one cleanup attempt may leave the staged entry behind. The test now uses the bounded `wait_for` helper to retry cleanup and still verifies the checkout and registration are removed. This follows the same accepted fix for another drain test in #4530.

The [failed feature powerset job](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/actions/runs/40644576267/job/122670315541) exercised the original assertion. The targeted test passes locally after the change. The full `cargo run -- hook pre-merge --yes` gate ran 5,463 tests and reported seven failures outside this test; some require socket operations unavailable in this sandbox. CI on this PR will provide the complete verification.
author: worktrunk-bot

title: fix(list): restore task progress in the loading footer
body:
Restore the completed/total task counter removed in #4333 while keeping the inventory and clipped-row counts. The initial frame says “loading details…” until the task plan exists, then shows `N/M tasks complete`, including results for off-screen rows. Progress comes first so it remains visible in narrow terminals; stalled loading keeps the counter and identifies pending work.

PTY regressions cover full and clipped tables at 150 and 60 columns, checking monotonic progress and matching totals. A gated summary task exercises the actual stall callback at `1/2` complete, then verifies progress reaches `2/2` after release. All 12 focused progress/stall tests passed, and live Leaf checks passed at 80 and 60 columns.

title: fix(claude): write hook markers without re-executing wt
body:
Claude Code marker hooks now write through the repository already discovered by the hook process. This removes the nested `wt config state marker` invocation and its repeat repository discovery and worktree listing. Marker events remain silent and keep their existing best-effort behavior; the regression test failed on the old Stop hook's stderr output and passes with the in-process write. The five Claude hook integration tests pass.

This addresses the synchronous process overhead. Async registrations still need ordered writes and Git config lock handling, so #4618 stays open for that work.

Refs #4618 — automated triage

title: chore: bump jdx/packslip from 1.11.0 to 1.11.1
body:
Bumps [jdx/packslip](https://github.com/jdx/packslip) from 1.11.0 to 1.11.1.
Release notes

Sourced from jdx/packslip's releases.

v1.11.1: Go module helpers for build targets, monorepo bundle names, and signer checks

The Go module (github.com/jdx/packslip/go) gets three helpers for Go release tools that publish packslips. Until now those tools had to reimplement packslip rules in their own code. The statement format stays release/v1, and nothing changes for existing callers.

Added

  • GoTarget holds one build's Go settings: GOARCH, GOARM, GOAMD64, GO386, GOARM64, GOMIPS, GOPPC64, GORISCV64, and FloatABI. Arch() returns the packslip architecture and Variant() returns the variant, using whichever setting applies to GOARCH. For arm, FloatABI takes Go's softfloat or hardfloat, or a Rust or Zig target ABI such as gnueabi or gnueabihf, and overrides any float option in GOARM. (#297, @​jdx)

    target := packslip.GoTarget{GOARCH: "amd64", GOAMD64: "v3"}
artifact.Arch = target.Arch()       // "x86_64"
artifact.Variant = target.Variant() // "v3"

  • BundleName(project, repo) returns the bundle asset name the spec assigns when several tools share one repository's release. For example, github.com/owner/repo/mytool becomes packslip.mytool.sigstore.json, and any / in a deeper subpath becomes -. The repository itself, or a project outside it, gets packslip.sigstore.json. The repository is matched without regard to case. (#297, @​jdx)

  • CheckProjectSigner(project, token) checks, before anything is signed or written to the transparency log, that an OIDC token can sign for the project. Call it after AmbientIDToken. A github.com project must belong to the token's repository claim, and a gitlab.com project must equal its project_path claim. A reusable workflow from another repository passes. A domain project always passes, because its vendor pins the signer. (#297, @​jdx)

title: feat(completion): complete remote-qualified switch branches
body:
Typing a remote prefix in `wt switch` now completes qualified remote-tracking branch names, including in repositories where the general completion list omits remote branches after the 100-candidate cutoff. Local branches literally named `origin/...` remain available. The existing unqualified completion behavior is unchanged.

The fish completion regression test failed before the change and now passes. Verified the 19 targeted switch completion tests, help snapshots, documentation sync, and docs build.

Closes #4612 — automated triage
author: worktrunk-bot

title: Prevent log permission repair from changing symlink targets
body:
Reject symlinked directories in the log tree before changing directory permissions. The permission helper added in #4604 used `set_permissions` on each path, which follows a symlink: a linked log directory could change an unrelated directory to mode `0700`. Creating descendants one level at a time also avoids writing through a nested directory link before it is checked.

The regression test covers a linked log root and a linked child directory. It failed before the fix and passes afterward. `cargo fmt --check` and the focused unit test pass. The full `cargo run -- hook pre-merge --yes` gate ran 5,462 tests: 5,455 passed, seven failed, and one was skipped. The failures include Unix socket creation blocked by this sandbox, shell-install snapshot path differences, and an SSH signing key mode error; I have not confirmed whether they reproduce on `main`.
author: worktrunk-bot

title: Serialize signal scope retirement with signal receipt
body:
A final alias child can catch Ctrl-C and exit successfully before wt's signal-owning thread finishes handling its SIGINT. Retiring the final foreground scope on another thread can restore idle default handling during that receipt, killing wt instead of preserving the child's exit status.

Retire foreground scopes on the existing process owner, which already serializes signal receipt with child admission. Add a controlled regression that pauses receipt while a real child handles Ctrl-C and exits successfully, cover nested owner requests and panic propagation, and preserve exit status and stderr in the alias test's failure diagnostic.

Includes the receipt handshake from [#4607](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/4607): the alias test keeps its child alive until wt records receiving SIGINT. This separates an interrupt received during the command from one that arrives after the child has exited. The controlled unit regression independently exercises teardown during an already-entered handler.

The regression fails against main and passes with the fix on Linux and macOS. Validation: full project gate (5,442 tests passed, one skipped), Linux signal/process-owner tests, and all 91 Linux alias tests.

Fixes #4603.

> _This was written by Codex on behalf of max-sixty_
author: max-sixty

title: Read the cd directive file as-is in every shell wrapper
body:
wt wrote the `cd` target followed by a newline, and each reader removed it its own way: fish, PowerShell and Nushell trimmed all surrounding whitespace, bash and zsh dropped trailing newlines, and wt's existence check from #4602 stripped line terminators. So a directory whose name ends in a space worked in bash and zsh but not in the other three.

wt now writes the bare path, and every reader takes the contents as-is: fish reads with `string collect`, PowerShell and Nushell drop their trims, and wt's existence check strips nothing. I checked all five wrappers `cd` into a directory named `dir ` (fish failed before).

A hand-written directive ending in a newline (a hook using `echo`) is now read with the newline included; wt's own writes and the tests already use the bare path.

> _This was written by Claude Code on behalf of max-sixty_
author: max-sixty

title: Keep legacy project approvals within SSH port boundaries
body:
A saved approval for `host.example/o/r` previously authorized project commands from `ssh://git@host.example:2222/o/r.git` through the legacy identifier fallback. Exclude legacy identifiers that lost the SSH port, including malformed SSH URLs, so approval lookup, project settings, and approval removal use the same server boundary. Safe hostname-case and raw `git+ssh` compatibility remain.

Non-default-port repositories must reapprove commands under their port-qualified ID and use that ID for project overrides. Regression coverage exercises refused exact and wildcard port-less approvals and successful port-qualified approval through a project alias.

Validation: regression failed before the fix and passes afterward; independent review found no issues; formatting, lint, documentation, and doctests passed. Full local suite: 5,440 passed, one detached-removal timeout; that case passed separately.

> _This was written by Codex on behalf of max-sixty_
author: max-sixty

title: Escape terminal controls in commit subjects and PR context
body:
Commit subjects and forge metadata could emit terminal commands in styled output, including OSC 52 clipboard sequences. Escape control bytes with the existing helper before truncating or styling the list message and PR/MR context. JSON retains the original subject.

Regression tests reproduce both input paths and verify that application styling remains enabled. Both also passed real 80-column xterm PTY probes. Independent review found no issues.

Local validation: linting, documentation, and doctests passed. The full gate ran 5,443 tests: 5,440 passed and three failed in foreground-process, fish-wrapper, and detached-removal tests outside the changed paths.

> _This was written by Codex on behalf of max-sixty_
author: max-sixty

title: Redact sensitive auth probe output and restrict log permissions
body:
Authentication probes print their credentials, which captured-output logging previously copied into debug logs, diagnostics, and stderr under `RUST_LOG=debug`. Add `Cmd::sensitive_output()` and apply it to GitHub and GitLab token probes so callers retain the original output while both subprocess logging targets emit `[redacted]`. Status and timing remain available, including for failed probes; pipelines propagate sensitivity to both commands.

Use one permission-preparation helper for debug, diagnostic, command-history, and background-hook logs. On Unix it applies `0600` to regular files and `0700` to log directories, including existing paths and command-log rotation. Initialization also secures existing active and rotated audit logs when the current command writes no audit entry. Permission repair handles read-only files without opening audit streams, so FIFOs cannot block initialization. Preserve native file-opening behavior for FIFO log destinations and keep `RUST_LOG` filtering consistent across full and bounded output.

Validation: the full project pre-merge gate passed with 5,446 tests passing and one skipped, plus formatting, Clippy, doctests, and rustdoc. Regression coverage checks fake credentials across all logging destinations, returned output, failures, concurrent commands, pipelines, and new/existing log permissions. Disabling redaction made all three auth-probe regression cases fail on leaked fake credentials.

> _This was written by Codex on behalf of max-sixty_
author: max-sixty

title: fix: don't cd into a directory removed before wt exits
body:
The shell wrapper acts on the cd directive only after wt exits, and work that runs in between can remove the directory it names. `wt switch -x` writes the directive before starting the program, so a program that removes its own worktree (an agent session that ends with `wt remove`) left the wrapper to `cd` into a missing directory: fish printed `cd: The directory '…' does not exist` and the wrapper returned failure. A hook or alias whose nested `wt switch` targets a worktree that a later step removes hits the same thing.

As wt finishes, `finish_command` now reads the directive file and empties it when the directory it names no longer exists, so the shell stays where it started. The outermost wt finishes last, after everything it runs in the foreground, so this one check covers every writer — the `-x` program, hooks, aliases, and nested wt — without touching the five shell wrappers. It is best-effort: if the file can't be read or emptied, the wrapper's own `cd` error still names the directory.

One behavior change: a hook that writes a directive naming a path that doesn't exist (a typo, say) used to surface a `cd` error; the shell now stays put silently. `test_concurrent_hooks_log_labels_and_pass_cd_directive` wrote a dummy `CD` target, so it now writes an existing directory.

Regression tests cover the `-x` case (`test_switch_execute_that_removes_worktree_withdraws_cd`) and the nested-hook case (`test_directive_to_worktree_removed_by_later_step_is_withdrawn`); both fail without the change.

title: fix(tether): propagate supervised command failures
body:
`wt step tether` returned success even when the command it supervised failed, which hid a failed dev server or other supervised task from scripts and hook logs. It now passes the command's exit status through when the command exits on its own. It still sweeps the process group first, and it uses the same child-status error as the other command runners. Two cases are not reported as a failure of the command:

- **Ctrl-C** exits silently as interrupted, by SIGINT. Cancellation is checked before the child status, as in `src/commands/custom.rs`.
- **Worktree removal** is tether's normal teardown, and it exits 0.

To make these distinctions, tether waits with `forward_to_children` plus `wait_shared_child` instead of `ForegroundSignals::wait`. The latter classifies any child that dies from SIGTERM as foreground cancellation, so tether's own teardown SIGTERM surfaced as an interruption (exit 143). Cancellation now counts only signals that `wt` itself received.

Verification: the `step_tether` integration tests cover all three outcomes. `sh -c 'exit 7'` exits 7. Removing the worktree exits 0. Ctrl-C exits by SIGINT with empty stderr. All five pass locally, and before the wait change the removal and Ctrl-C assertions failed with exit 143. The `child.wait()` I/O-error arm is uncovered, which the maintainer accepted.

Update the Tend workflows from 0.3.15 through 0.3.22. The earlier commits replace the dedicated CI fix path with one failure report and let triage continue independent repairs when a case has several causes. title: Serialize signal receipt with foreground child admission
body:
Ctrl-C during concurrent hook startup could leave `wt` waiting forever after an existing child finished cleanup. If the kernel assigned SIGINT to another thread and delayed its handler, the spawning thread could admit children that missed both the terminal signal and the cancellation checks.

Initialize one Unix thread that owns signal receipt and process creation. Other threads inherit blocked SIGINT/SIGTERM; the owner and its children retain the inherited mask. Run foreground admission checks on that owner, preserving cleanup for previously admitted children. Child execution and waits remain concurrent. Library callers that omit early startup initialization retain their existing direct-spawn behavior.

Reproduced the failure on both the reported revision and current main by pausing native SIGINT delivery with Linux ptrace: late shell children survived after `CLEANUP_FINISHED`, and `wt` timed out waiting for them. Under the repair, the same pause admitted no additional children and the command exited with 130 after cleanup. This reproduces the reported failure mode; the original CI log alone cannot establish its precise scheduling history.

Validation:
- Linux project validation: 5,476 tests, pre-commit/Clippy, lockfile, docs, and doctests (one configured skipped test). Two process-group tests required rerunning unchanged with Docker `--init` so orphaned children were reaped.
- Regression test delays signal handling while another thread attempts admission; it also checks child masks and reusable commands. Bypassing owner routing makes it fail with “child started before signal receipt finished”; restoring the repair passes.
- Native spawn tests cover in-flight TERM cancellation, cancellation overriding an exec failure, and recovery after an owner request panics; both affected tests pass on macOS.
- Linux foreground suite: 82 passed, including real bash, zsh, fish, and Nushell jobs.
- Paired Linux `wt list` timing: baseline median 21.36 ms, repair 21.28 ms over 20 alternating samples each (nine worktrees, four dirty).

Closes #4511.

title: Simplify shell integration detection to known setup lines
body:
Shell integration detection used partial shell-syntax heuristics to decide whether an entire rc-file line belonged to Worktrunk. An alias quoting initialization, or an initialization followed by another command, could therefore be removed by uninstall.

Recognize complete generated, documented, and historical setup forms instead. Current installer lines come directly from the generator; install, diagnostics, and uninstall share the matcher, which also supplies the shell identity. Preserve custom command names, `.exe` names, Git dispatch, and older installer forms without adding a parser dependency. Remove the syntax-variation heuristics and their tests.

Customized shell expressions remain user-managed: uninstall leaves them alone, diagnostics explain that boundary, and installing over such a setup may append the standard initialization line. Regression coverage checks install idempotency and preservation of quoted aliases and compound statements.

Validation: shell unit and install/uninstall integration tests, independent CLI lifecycle probes, help snapshots, documentation sync/build, doctests, and all pre-commit checks pass. The full local gate ran 5,430 tests with 5,422 passing. Its documentation-sync failure was resolved by regeneration and a passing repeat; remaining failures were an unchanged startup test, two process-discovery preconditions, and four PowerShell-related failures. The installed `pwsh` also stack-overflows on standalone `1 + 1`, independently of Worktrunk. CI must pass before merge.

Closes #4106.

title: chore: bump jdx/packslip from 1.7.0 to 1.11.0
body:
Bumps [jdx/packslip](https://github.com/jdx/packslip) from 1.7.0 to 1.11.0.
Release notes

Sourced from jdx/packslip's releases.

v1.11.0: Repository-bound signer checks for GitHub and GitLab projects, install fallback, and empty release lists

packslip 1.11.0 makes every verifier in the repository (the CLI, the npm package, and the committable verifier) require a github.com or gitlab.com project to be signed from its own repository. It also makes packslip install fall back to older releases, warn about withdrawn installs, and stop raising some unnecessary trust-change prompts. The format stays at release/v1: the specification changes clarify existing rules, write down how the reference implementations already behave, and settle one conflict between icon rules. No change requires a new format version.

Security

  • Identity flags now narrow a forge project's signer policy instead of replacing it (#256, @​jdx). packslip verify derives a signer policy from a GitHub or GitLab project's name. Before this release, --issuer, --identity, or --identity-prefix replaced that policy. As a result, passing only GitHub Actions' OIDC issuer to --issuer accepted a bundle claiming github.com/owner/tool that any GitHub repository had signed. Now the certificate must also tie the signer to the project's repository. A reusable workflow from another repository still passes when the project's own run called it. Projects on other hosts are unaffected: for them, the flags are still the whole policy.
  • New verify --allow-other-repository accepts a document signed outside the project's repository on purpose, such as a repackager's. You must also pass --issuer and name the signer with --identity, --identity-prefix, or --source-repository. The option is refused with --pubkey. 
    packslip verify packslip.sigstore.json \
  --issuer "$GITHUB_OIDC_ISSUER" \
  --identity-prefix "$REPACKAGER_WORKFLOW_PREFIX" \
  --allow-other-repository
    The jdx/packslip/releases action gains an allow-other-repository input (default false). It passes the flag automatically when project names a repository other than the one running the action, as with a registry's list.
  • The committable verifier (verifier/packslip-verify.mjs) applies the same repository rule to a github.com or gitlab.com --project (#258,

title: Retain partial JSON results when later command steps fail
body:
Preserve confirmed work in JSON output when a later command step fails. For example, a switch that creates a worktree before `--execute` fails still reports the created path; push and merge retain a completed target update if final verification fails. Command payloads stay on stdout, readable diagnostics stay on stderr, and the exit status signals failure.

Carry typed partial facts across mutation boundaries and serialize them in the command handlers. This covers switch, commit/squash, merge/push, remove/prune, relocation, and copy-ignored without adding a public result/error envelope. Switch failures before any result exists now leave stdout empty instead of returning an error-only JSON object. Help and regression tests document the contract.

Validation: 309 focused tests and nine additional boundary cases passed, including late commit/squash, prune, relocation, and detached-removal failures and skipped-copy accounting. Clippy, pre-commit, documentation checks, and doctests passed. The full local gate had 12 failures: nine passed sequentially, while three PowerShell tests reproduced `Stack overflow.`. After integrating current main, all-target/all-feature compilation and a review of the overlapping changes passed. CI remains the merge gate.

title: fix(shell): configure remaining shells after an rc file error
body:
A UTF-16 `.bashrc` stopped the install scan before it reached later shells, leaving PowerShell integration unconfigured. `wt config shell install` now records rc-file errors and continues configuring other shells; it leaves the unreadable file untouched, reports partial failure with a nonzero exit, and identifies a UTF-16 byte-order mark with a re-save hint. The first-run shell prompt also reports a file that becomes unreadable after confirmation. Path-resolution failures still stop the scan, since a missing home blocks every shell and a cancelled PowerShell profile query must stop the command.

A regression test with a UTF-16 `.bashrc` and a valid `.zshrc` failed before the change and now confirms zsh installs while Bash remains unchanged. A second test covers an rc file becoming invalid during the first-run prompt. The existing single-shell read-error test also passes. These tests exercise the shared install path on Linux; I have not run the Windows PowerShell profile flow.

Closes #4582 — automated triage
